---
title: "An image with no caption"
description: "An image with no caption floats to the right and keeps its alt text."
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
  typst:
    output-file: uncaptioned-image-typst.pdf
  docx: default
---

The image on this page has no caption and no id, so it gets no figure
number:

```markdown
![](badge.png){.wrap-right width="20%" fig-alt="A round blue badge with the letter w"}
```

## Result

A badge, a logo, or an icon often has no caption and no number. This
section uses one such image, and this paragraph comes before it, so it
runs the full width of the text.

![](../images/badge.png){.wrap-right width="20%" fig-alt="A round blue badge with the letter w"}

An image with no caption wraps in the same way as a captioned figure. The
class `.wrap-right` puts it on the right, and the text flows on its left.
The image is 20% of the text width, so the text beside it keeps most of
the line. A small image like this one suits a logo or an icon at the start
of a section. The image has no number, so the text cannot point to it
with a `@fig-` link. The `width` attribute sets only the width, and the
height follows from the image's shape, so this square image is as tall as
it is wide. Because the image is short, the text passes its bottom before
the end of this paragraph. From there on, each line runs the full width of the text,
under the image. In HTML and Word, the `fig-alt` attribute gives the image
its alt text, which a screen reader reads in place of the image. In a PDF,
alt text needs a tagged PDF (see the format pages).
